articles.headline: Sawalich Nips Perkins at the Line to Win Daytona Opener
articles.dek: A last-lap charge off turn four gives William Sawalich the United Rentals 300 victory by 0.077 seconds.
articles.body:
DAYTONA BEACH, Fla. - William Sawalich edged Blaine Perkins by 0.077 seconds at Daytona International Speedway on Saturday, taking the season-opening United Rentals 300 in a dash to the line.

Sawalich started 25th and led only two laps in the No. 18, but timed his run off turn four on the 48th and final lap to drag-race Perkins to the checkered flag. Cleetus McFarland finished third, while Daniel Dye charged through the field from 32nd to take fourth. Brent Crews completed the top five.

"We bided our time near the back early and let everybody burn their stuff up," Sawalich said. "When the hole opened on the high side coming off turn four, I just stayed in the throttle. Getting one early takes a ton of pressure off this team."

The 48-lap race featured 15 lead changes among 12 drivers under clear, 51-degree skies. Pole sitter Jesse Love struggled to maintain track position in the draft, eventually sliding back to finish 21st.

Ryan Sieg and Parker Retzlaff did the heavy lifting out front through the afternoon. Sieg paced the field for a race-high 17 laps, while Retzlaff led 12 circuits. Both drivers found themselves shuffled backward during the final cycle of moves, with Retzlaff finishing seventh and Sieg crossing the stripe in eighth.

Perkins led two laps late and appeared positioned to hold off the outside lane entering the tri-oval, but Sawalich found clean air off the bumper of the trailing pack.

"Missed it by less than a tenth," Perkins said. "The 18 had a huge run off four and I tried to pinch him down, but he had too much momentum. Second hurts on a superspeedway, but it is solid points to open the year."

Two cautions slowed the event, keeping the 38-car grid bunched up. Several contenders hit trouble during the afternoon, with four drivers failing to make the finish. Ryan Ellis retired early due to an ignition failure, while Mason Maggio, Kyle Sieg, and Josh Williams pulled out of competition before the final restart.

The attrition and pack racing opened lanes for drivers starting deep in the order. In addition to Sawalich and Crews advancing from outside the top 20, Austin Green surged from 34th to finish sixth, Andrew Patterson went from 35th to ninth, and Sammy Smith rebounded from starting 38th to crack the top 10.

Dye made the biggest climb of the day, gaining 28 positions over 48 laps without pacing a single circuit.

"Starting thirty-second you just have to be smart and miss the mess," Dye said. "We picked them off three or four at a time on the restarts and the car had plenty of speed in clean air. P4 is a great start."

Sawalich leaves Daytona leading the standings with 40 points and an early win in the bank. Perkins ranks second with 35 points, followed by McFarland with 34, Dye with 33, and Crews with 32. Green (31), Retzlaff (30), Sieg (29), Patterson (28), and Smith (27) round out the top 10.

The series continues its 33-race schedule next week for round two.

articles.headline: One More Day: Austin Hill Eyes Another Daytona Opener
articles.dek: The NASCAR on JRN Xfinity Series season opens tomorrow at Daytona with Austin Hill chasing his fifth season-opening win in six years.
articles.body:
The wait is nearly over for the NASCAR on JRN Xfinity Series as the field prepares for the United Rentals 300 at Daytona International Speedway. Coverage begins at 5 PM ET on JRN on February 14th, 2026, marking the official start of a new simulated racing campaign.

All eyes point directly at Austin Hill as the green flag approaches. Hill enters the season opener as the driver to beat after dominating Speedweeks over recent years, capturing four of the last five season-opening victories at the historic 2.5-mile superspeedway. His recent history at Daytona establishes him as the undisputed favorite to control the draft and defend his ongoing restrictor-plate dynasty.

With zero races in the books, the standings remain a blank slate, leaving every team on equal footing before tomorrow afternoon. The draft packs, single-file freight trains, and late-race shuffling will dictate who survives the chaotic opening laps and positions themselves for a shot at the trophy.

Teams face their final technical inspections this morning before final practices wrap up. The drivers know the superspeedway drafting dynamics leave zero room for error, and the race on JRN will set the competitive baseline for the entire 2026 season.
articles.author: Ross Delgado

posts.text: Cloudy and 70 degrees here in Daytona with a 16 mph northeast breeze. Sam Mayer tops the lone practice session at 46.660 over Jesse Love (46.697) and Taylor Gray (46.715). All 38 cars took times.
Love ran that second-best lap completely in dirty air too. If the grill isn't ruined by rain tomorrow the 2 car is gonna be tough to beat.
Gray was only .055 off Mayer in his first superspeedway hit with the 54 group. That car has speed.
Dean Thompson P4 right behind them at 46.721. My fantasy lineup is locked in. Easy cash.
Lavar Scott fifth in practice means very little when track position goes away on lap 30 and your pit crew gives up four spots on green flag stops.
He held a clean line in the draft for twenty laps and kept the nose clean. We take P5 and move on.

posts.title: Daytona practice speeds - real draft speed or single car outliers?
posts.text: Woke up still feeling last night just to see Ryan Ellis sitting P6 at 46.808. Daytona practice charts are basically fiction but seeing Clements and Poole in the top eight is wild.
poole only got p8 because he caught the tail of the rcr pack lol bro was invisible before that
Ellis and Clements hooked up for a two-car tandem run late in the session when ambient temps cooled slightly. That explains the jump, but Ellis maintained 185.3 mph for three straight laps.
People read too much into top times. Jesse Love put up 46.697 in a pack of six cars without any bump drafting. That 2 team worked strictly on fuel run simulation today.
Dean Thompson ran 46.721 mostly leading the third line while the 2 rode around saving fuel. You guys hype Love up for literally breathing.
He qualified second in speed without tearing up a nose. I have to be at the job site Monday morning and I just want a race without five red flags, Love has the car to control the field.
He'll control the field right into the outside wall on lap 45.
Back when the cars had real carburetors you found out who had horsepower on Saturday afternoon not in some twenty-car train on Friday. But I'll still be glued to the tv like every February.
DAYTONA PRACTICE OVER. Mayer and Love look hooked up, but do NOT sleep on Cleetus McFarland in P20 (46.970). Full breakdown dropping on the channel tonight before qualifying!
p20 in a 38 car field is not the flex you think it is 💀
thompson p4 fr
All this talk about the midfield and nobody is mentioning Ryan Ellis will probably fall out of the draft before stage 1 finishes. Every single year.
Ellis ran top six speed cleanly while half the field was throwing wild blocks on an overcast Friday afternoon. Give the smaller teams some credit.

posts.title: Sawalich P9 vs Creed P10 - who do you trust more tomorrow?
posts.text: Sawalich put down a 46.885 and Creed was right behind at 46.903. Creed had the faster 5-lap average but you know one of them is causing a twelve-car pileup by lap 60. Who we fading?
Neither of them knows how to draft without shoving the guy ahead through the trioval. The stages ruined patience at Daytona twenty years ago. Miss the 500-mile grinds where you paced yourself.
Creed seemed to handle better when the wind picked up out of the northeast. That 00 was planted while Sawalich had the rear wiggling coming off four. We'll see how the track takes rubber tomorrow.
CLEETUS MCFARLAND 46.970... car looked great in the turns. remids me of the 90s independent runners building their own stuff. real racers
bro cleetus was 20th let it go
twenty cars within three tenths... he beat Perkins and Burton. watch the race kid
Sawalich was 46.885 in practice and looked sideways every time someone pulled to his door. Going to be a long 300 miles if he doesn't calm down on the wheel.
jeb burton p14 is actually so solid people aren't understanding how hard that car is to drive in 16mph winds
kyle sieg barely cracked p11 at 46.909 bro thought he was gonna lead the draft 💀
Track was cold and slick all afternoon. Anyone who stayed off the fence did their job today, nothing to read into tenths of a second at Daytona.

posts.title: Big Lou Marchetti pre-race radio segment notes
posts.text: Talked to a few crew chiefs in the garage after that overcast session. Consensus is simple: 16 mph crosswind off turn 2 made these cars evil on entry. Watch the bottom lane get bogged down if they can't get three cars linked up.

LOU you nailed it... the cars wander too much now... back when the ride height rule existed they stuck to the track... now it looks like an interstate traffic jam. CAUTION after CAUTION tomorrow watch
Just praying the broadcast doesn't stay on in-car cameras for forty laps while the pack is three-wide. Still nursing a hangover from Thursday night and that shaky cam will end me.
Put five bucks on Perkins at huge odds just because he held 46.968 alone without drafting help late. Need that lottery ticket to hit.
Blaine Perkins P19 at 46.968 ahead of McFarland and Harrison Burton. Keep that up in qualifying and we have a fighting chance for stage points tomorrow.
LOOK at the bottom of the board... Byrd Maggio Bilicki over a second off... gonna get lapped early... dangerous in the draft. - D
Dean Thompson 46.721 still rent free across everyone's timeline. Top five starting spot incoming.
Thompson had a tow from two Kaulig cars, settle down. Lavar Scott did almost the identical time with zero drafting partner and nobody's crowning him.
Scott was P5 because he drafted Mayer for three laps check the sector times before typing
Justin Allgaier takes the pole for the United Rentals 300 with a 47.028 lap. Jesse Love lines up beside him at 47.043. Austin Hill third.
Front row start for Love. Allgaier will fade once the draft gets moving and Jesse controls the high side. Need him to wrap it up early before I have to prep the grill for family on Sunday.
He qualified second because RCR builds rocket ships on restrictor plate tracks... wait until lap 40 when he tries to squeeze three wide and finds the wall... seen it before. - D
He held 46.697 in practice second fastest behind Mayer with zero drafting help. Keep complaining while he leads fifty laps.
Practice speeds mean zero at Daytona. He will fumble the lead on the first green flag pit sequence. - D
Second row has Hill right behind Jesse so they will hook up on the restart regardless. Nothing to panic over either way ¯\_(ツ)_/¯

posts.title: Qualifying Results Discussion - United Rentals 300
posts.text: Qualifying showed the expected single-car aerodynamic strengths. The top five separated by just 0.040 seconds: Allgaier (47.028), Love (47.043), Hill (47.055), B. Jones (47.058), Kvapil (47.068). Notable disparity: Taylor Gray was P3 in practice drafting (46.715) but fell to P17 in solo trim (47.339).
Single car runs mean almost nothing for the actual 300 miles. Gray will draft right back up to the top ten inside twenty laps while Jones drops like an anchor.

It matters for pit stall selection though. Getting a clean exit off pit road without checking up on entry will dictate who survives stage two. Got a brisket going on the smoker right now so hopefully no dumb yellow flags stretch this out.
Jesse on row one is massive. The spotter has a clean view into turn one and he won't be trapped in dirty air when the mid-pack accordion happens on lap 15.
Ryan Sieg put the 39 in tenth at 47.210. Good solid starting spot without tearing up equipment. That team builds their own stuff and deserves more respect than these kids renting rides. - D

Poole back in 18th at 47.408 because these spec chassis all drive identical in the turbulence. Back in 1994 a guy could build a better nose in the shop and jump five tenths. Now it is all governed down.
It is Daytona qualifying. The spread between 1st and 20th is four tenths of a second. The pack will reshuffle on lap 3 anyway ¯\_(ツ)_/¯
jeb burton p38 literally dead last what actually happened to the car im sick to my stomach
bro had a 46.939 in practice and then forgot how to run a straight line 💀
he had a massive headwind on his run and the team missed the tape on the nose it is NOT his fault he will pass twenty cars in ten laps watch
Sure Jan. Even Corey Day managed P13 in practice while Burton is busy parking next to Cram and Fenhaus on the grid.
p38 is wild 💀
ALLGAIER TAKES POLE AT DAYTONA. But do not sleep on Cleetus McFarland starting P13 in the 33 car! Full race breakdown going live on my channel tonight, you will NOT want to miss my dark horse pick.

Justin proved the veteran savvy matters. Kept it pinned on the yellow line all the way through three and four. Nice to start up front for once, off to get the grill ready for Monday work week ¯\_(ツ)_/¯
McFarland qualified 47.297 ahead of Thompson, Alfredo, and Sawalich. Fox will spend forty laps showing his tachometer instead of the battle for the lead.
Sawalich starting 16th behind Cleetus is pure comedy. Watching with my boy and we both laughed when that 47.336 popped up. Zero racecraft on these high banks ¯\_(ツ)_/¯
dean thompson was p4 in practice bro he will be fine

posts.title: Anyone else hitting the betting slips based on practice times?
posts.text: If you looked at practice times to set your fantasy lineup please log off. Sam Mayer topped practice at 46.660 because he drafted off Scott and Gray, then Qualified 7th at 47.130. Don't fall for the draft tow trap.
woke up with a massive headache but still locked in Austin Hill top 3 at plus money. starting P3 at 47.055 is basically a gift for how good that 21 pushes.
Perkins at 47.408 in P19 is the sneaky fantasy value. He was 46.968 alone in practice yesterday without a tow. If he stays clean he gets stage points easily.

Betting slips and fantasy points have ruined how folks talk about Daytona... nobody cares about who can actually wheel the car off four anymore. The points stages give freebies to guys riding in the back. Still the greatest track in the country and nobody can change that.
RockinghamDon complaining about fantasy points while watching guys ride around at 60 percent throttle is peak boomer behavior.
bro rajah caruth p9 at 47.187 is right there in the mix people sleeping on the 88 fr

Overcast sky at 66 degrees gave these cars all the grip in the world during qualifying. But tomorrow the sun comes out and that Northeast wind at 17 miles per hour is going to push cars right into the wall off turn two. Hold on to your hats.
Spot on Lou... winds off the ocean always played havoc with the handling back in the eighties before all this telemetry told them what to do. The boys better respect the draft. - B
Told my boy while we were watching qualifying that track conditions change everything. Poole sitting 18th in the 44 car is right where you want to be to dodge the early mess ¯\_(ツ)_/¯
Lavar Scott was fifth in practice at 46.801 but could not back it up when the wind picked up. If his spotter doesn't manage pit entry under green he will lose two laps immediately.
three cups of coffee deep and already dreading the commercial-to-green-flag ratio. just let them race through turn two without cutting to a truck commercial.
starting on pole just to finish twenty first is a tough look for the twenty car today. guess we have to go back to the drawing board before next weekend. - b
pole position doesn't mean much when the setup falls off over a long run. we will clean it up for the next one. grill is lit though so whatever. - m
POLE SITTERS NEVER WIN ANYWAY back in my day they actually raced instead of saving fuel all afternoon... - D

posts.title: United Rentals 300 post race thoughts
posts.text: another superspeedway race decided on the last lap... cars all look identical out there now too can barely tell 'em apart without the numbers blasted on the roof...
aint that the truth... back in ninety five you could tell every make from the sound alone... now it's just pack racing and green white checkered nonsense...
at least the racing at the end was clean enough compared to what we usually see here. time to fire up the grill and pretend my monday morning meetings aren't happening.
agreed on the grill part at least. starting thirty second to finish fourth like dye did was the most impressive drive of the whole afternoon. - th
William Sawalich wins the United Rentals 300 at Daytona by 0.077 seconds over Blaine Perkins after a charge on the high side off turn four.
woke up with the worst hangover of my life and watching perkins finish second by a bumper almost made me lose the rest of my coffee. hell of a points day though.

posts.title: Cleetus and the superspeedway draft
posts.text: cleetus p3 after starting eighteenth is honestly hilarious. fox must have been losing their minds every time he crossed the start finish line.
anyone complaining about media coverage needs to remember he brings eyes to the Xfinity series. my boy jesse will get his time back soon enough.
the broadcast talked about him way too much when parker retzlaff was leading twelve laps and actually working the draft. pit strategy on the nine-nine needed help though.
retzlaff had a solid run going until the very end. hard to fault the execution when the whole field is three wide on white flag lap. - brian
Daniel Dye quietly posted the biggest mover award today, advancing 28 positions from P32 to P4 with zero recorded incidents. Clean execution in dirty air.
dye actually drove a smart race from the back while everyone else was tearing up equipment. consistency wins championships.
SAWALICH STOLE THAT ONE OFF FOUR!! What an absolute heater to start the year in Daytona!!
retzlaff led a dozen laps and got shuffled out at the end while everyone else got a lucky draft. pain.

posts.title: Daytona Xfinity opener breakdown
posts.text: Reminds me of the old days when guys had to actually muscle these stock cars through the banking instead of just locking bumpers and praying. Sawalich drove a clean line at the end though, credit where it is due.
lou hits the nail on the head. playoff format still rewards survival over winning races outright but at least the eighteen earned that pass.

interviews.quote: Starting thirty-second you just have to be smart and miss the mess. We picked them off three or four at a time on the restarts and the car had plenty of speed in clean air. P4 is a great start.
Missed it by less than a tenth. The 18 had a huge run off four and I tried to pinch him down, but he had too much momentum. Second hurts on a superspeedway, but it is solid points to open the year.

We bided our time near the back early and let everybody burn their stuff up. When the hole opened on the high side coming off turn four, I just stayed in the throttle. Getting one early takes a ton of pressure off this team.

events.why: Executed a clean high-side pass off turn four to win at the line.
Praised the team and showed poise winning from 25th on the grid.
Drove cleanly from 32nd to 4th without incident.
Kept his head down and methodically drove forward through the field.
Charged from P32 to P4 at United Rentals 300
Took the close loss with class while acknowledging a strong points day.
Charged from P37 to P14 at Bennett Transport & Logistics 250

chase.headline: Opening Chase Projections Carry Little Weight
chase.summary: With only one race in the books out of thirty three, our simulation model has very little data to process, making most early odds closely clustered. William Sawalich leads the current playoff probability at ninety one percent with forty points, while Jeremy Clements sits on the cutline at twelve percent with fifteen points.

notes.william sawalich: Sawalich sits atop the early standings with forty points and a ninety one percent Chase probability following his latest win.
notes.jeremy clements: Clements finds himself at the bottom of the current projection list with twelve percent odds and fifteen points after one event.

race.headline: Superspeedway Chaos Awaits at EchoPark
race.summary: We are heading to the Bennett Transport and Logistics 250 at EchoPark Speedway where William Sawalich, Sammy Smith, and Parker Retzlaff top the win odds at nine and seven percent. Meanwhile, Ryan Ellis and Kyle Sieg lead the wreck risk category at a massive fifty six percent.

notes.ryan ellis: Ellis carries a race high fifty six percent wreck risk into the superspeedway showdown.
notes.william sawalich: Sawalich enters as the win favorite at nine percent after taking the checkered flag last time out.

season.headline: Early Projections Mirror Last Week
season.summary: Looking down the season projection after just one race is like reading tea leaves, but the numbers currently point to William Sawalich taking fourth with seven hundred forty six points and twenty two percent title odds. Blaine Perkins is slated right behind in fifth with seven hundred thirty four points and sixteen percent title odds.

notes.william sawalich: The model has Sawalich projected to finish fourth with a twenty two percent chance at the title.
notes.anthony alfredo: Alfredo rounds out the current twelve drivers projected to make the Chase with seven hundred fifty seven points.
